text:
Maya: Heads-up — we need a decision on per-key burst handling for heavy multi-tenant spikes. Do we prefer early 429s, or let requests queue and fall back to 503s later? Also thinking about how penalties/credits propagate across keys.
CJ: TL;DR I lean early 429 for tail latency predictability. Queues hide problems and can blow up. :thinking:
David: Agree on predictability, but early 429s can be noisy for bursty clients that are trying legitimate work. We have burst credits already though — can we surface them in console first?
Samir: We have two knobs: token-bucket burst credits and soft-queue with early drop. Proposal: short smoothing window (200–500ms) + preserve burst credits per-key, then early drop once burst credit exhausted.
Maya: Smoothing window + per-key credits sounds reasonable. What about per-org vs per-key hierarchy? We saw a tenant hogging keys but distributed across many keys.
CJ: Hierarchy: enforce per-key but also an org-level drain/fairness counter. If org aggregate > X, we throttle org-level. Per-key credits shouldn't allow org to exceed org cap.
David: Important: telemetry. We need signal for "credit burn rate" and "soft-queue depth by key" in the console. Otherwise SREs chase ghosts.
Samir: On fallback semantics: if we shed early -> return 429 with headers: `X-Redwood-Shed: early`, `X-Burst-Credits-Left: <n>`. If we queue and later evict -> 503 with `X-Redwood-Shed: evicted-queue`. Keep these machine-readable.
Eve: Can we try a feature-flag rollout? Start with 10% orgs: enable smoothing window + headers, track error budgets and client-side retrys. Deploy bot will tag canary.
InfraBot: deploy:rollout started for feature flag `smoothing-burst-v1` to 10% orgs at 2026-03-18T15:12:03Z.
CJ: UX note: console should show per-route shed rate and a histogram of `X-Burst-Credits-Left` values over last 1h. Also a per-org heatmap for aggregated sheds.
Maya: Good. One more: penalty propagation. If a key gets 429s, do we decay its credits faster? I suggest linear backoff on credit refill (multiply refill interval by 2 on each continuous shed event up to 8x), so aggressive abusers get slower recovery.
David: Love the exponential refill backoff. Let's also attach a reason code in the response body (short code like `SHEd:ORG_OVERAGE`), so clients and internal telemetry can correlate.
Samir: Implementation notes: token-bucket per key, org aggregator that samples top 1% heavy keys, smoothing queue implemented on router with capacity 500ms per request, eviction priority = oldest + lowest credits, emit `shed_reason` tag in tracing.
Eve: A/B plan: Flag A (current behavior) vs Flag B (smoothing + early 429 + backoff). Metrics to watch: p99 latency, customer error rate, retry amplification (retry storms), and active queue depth.
Maya: Ok next steps: Samir/Infra to prototype smoothing in the router, CJ to spec console metrics and header schema, David to draft telemetry + dashboard widgets, Eve to coordinate rollout plan and canary. We'll reconvene in 48h. :thumbsup:
